claims.text: Laser surface alloying with pre-placed CoCrFeNiMo-based HEA powder can repair or improve damaged 316L stainless-steel surfaces.
A low-energy pulsed laser can melt the pre-placed HEA powder together with only a thin surface layer of the 316L substrate.
Controlled laser energy density and scan speed under an inert atmosphere will provide rapid and uniform solidification.
Rapid laser-induced solidification will produce a refined, metastable dendritic microstructure.
The resulting microstructure will contain a fine mixture of FCC and BCC phases.
The refined FCC/BCC microstructure will result in low residual stress and minimal defect formation.
Localized melting and rapid solidification will create a homogeneous, crack-resistant HEA-alloyed surface layer.
Limiting thermal exposure will reduce the hot cracking associated with traditional fusion-welding repair.
The HEA-alloyed layer will increase surface hardness.
The HEA-alloyed layer will improve wear resistance.
The HEA-alloyed layer will improve corrosion resistance.
The laser-alloyed surface will have lower hot-cracking susceptibility than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The laser-alloyed surface will have greater hardness than both a traditional fusion-welded repair and an untreated 316L surface.
The laser-alloyed surface will have greater wear resistance than both a traditional fusion-welded repair and an untreated 316L surface.
The laser-alloyed surface will have greater corrosion resistance than both a traditional fusion-welded repair and an untreated 316L surface.
Traditional fusion-welded repairs typically exhibit more hot cracking and lower surface durability.
The proposed process is applicable primarily to 316L components requiring only a thin repaired surface layer and precise control of laser parameters.
Complex geometries and cyclic thermal or mechanical loading may limit scale-up and long-term durability.
